home.text:
Brand Designer · Offenburg, Germany

Hi, I’m Mona.

I make brands feel clear & human.

I design visual identities, useful guidelines and content that brings a brand to life – on screen and beyond.

8+ years in design. Currently at Shine, previously at sevdesk. I care about coherent brands and giving teams the tools to keep them that way.

Explore my work ↓

Get in touch ↗

Selected work

Brands in practice.

Four ways I turn a visual identity into something people can use, recognise and connect with.

01 / Guidelines · Documentation · Brand rollout

Brand guidelines

A clear foundation for a consistent brand.

sevdesk: Co-developed and maintained guidelines; supported the 2025 rebrand.
Shine: Refining existing guidelines and making them easier for teams to apply.

View brand guidelines →

02 / Merch Design · Booth assets · Brand application

Merch & brand experience

From screen to something tangible.

Created branded merchandise and offline touchpoints, including a trade fair experience for Shine.

View merch & brand experience →

03 / Social design · Templates · Creative delivery

Paid & organic content

One brand. Many formats and markets.

Designed paid and organic assets, built 50+ Figma Buzz templates and enabled 4+ teams to create on-brand content.

View paid & organic content →

04 / Visual exploration · Curation · Brand consistency

AI-assisted imagery

New tools. Same care for consistency.

Used AI for on-brand imagery, illustrations and layouts while keeping the visual direction consistent.

View ai-assisted imagery →

Away from keyboard

When I close my laptop, design doesn’t leave.

I keep seeking it out because it fills me with joy and fuels my creativity. I take photos, draw and visit museums. What I love most is discovering work that looks effortless, then learning through my own attempts how much skill and craft it takes to execute an idea well. That respect for craft carries into everything I design.

Let’s talk

Want to know more about my work?

monaschmidt.design@gmail.com ↗

I help turn a visual identity into clear, practical guidance – so a brand stays consistent as the company grows.
Co-developed and maintained guidelines; supported the 2025 rebrand.
Helping refine existing guidelines through asset creation, gap documentation and template rules.
Putting a refreshed brand into practice.
As part of the in-house design team, I helped implement the new brand elements, documented how to use them and kept their application consistent.
MY ROLE  /  Rebrand implementation · Documentation · Onboarding · Quality control
sevdesk · The brand identity our team helped implement and document.
Our team worked on applying the refreshed colour palette, new illustrations and shapes – including shapes used as background motifs or animated components.
Turn the assets into shared guidelines

We first documented usage guidelines in zeroheight, then moved to Standards as our company-wide single source of truth. A Figma overview supported the migration; the logo package and font were available to download from Standards.
During the documentation process and afterwards, we used this foundation to create paid and organic content, merchandise and illustrations.
I monitored internal and external use of our brand visuals – checking, for example, that the logo was not distorted, recoloured or otherwise used incorrectly.

Illustration · Shapes · Icons ·
Image style · Look & feel
I supported reviews of the sevdesk PowerPoint deck for completeness and ease of use. I also helped onboard new employees to the brand guidelines.

Our team organised production assets in Microsoft SharePoint, with a clear folder structure and regularly updated asset libraries. Standards remained the single source of truth for the brand guidelines.
I'm contributing to Shine’s evolving guidelines and asset library. As I create assets using the existing brand system, I document what we have, what is missing and what we could use next.
MY ROLE  /  Asset creation · Gap documentation · Template guidelines
What creating assets is teaching us
Creating assets has shown us that the existing illustration set does not yet cover everything we want to communicate in the product or in advertising.
We noticed an over-reliance on two brand colours and a need to bring in more hues. This led to gradients that we are currently developing, refining and documenting together as a team.
Create → Identify gaps → Refine together → Document
The work is ongoing: practical needs from asset creation inform how we build out the library and develop the guidelines.
I create templates based on the brand guidelines and document precise usage rules for these templates together with my design colleagues.

Building on what exists.

Documenting what’s next.

MY ROLE  /  Asset creation · Gap documentation · Template guidelines

What creating assets is teaching us

Illustration coverage

Creating assets has shown us that the existing illustration set does not yet cover everything we want to communicate in the product or in advertising.

Colour & gradients

We noticed an over-reliance on two brand colours and a need to bring in more hues. This led to gradients that we are currently developing, refining and documenting together as a team.

Create → Identify gaps → Refine together → Document

The work is ongoing: practical needs from asset creation inform how we build out the library and develop the guidelines.

paragraphs.text: I use AI to explore imagery, illustrations and layouts – while keeping the creative thinking and judgement my own.
Visual exploration, curation and on-brand application
Supporting high-output brand and marketing work
Image generation with Midjourney based on our sevdesk guidelines.
AI is part of my toolkit, not a replacement for a clear idea. I use it to amplify what I’m already doing: exploring visual directions and creating imagery that feels consistent with the brand.
At sevdesk, I have used Midjourney and Nano Banana for on-brand imagery, illustrations, icons, layouts and UI elements to support high output demands while maintaining a consistent look and feel.
How I put AI to work
Explore visual directions and create assets with a coherent brand feel.
I also use image generation to expand our stock library. My takeaway: well-crafted AI imagery can feel far more on-brand than even carefully curated images from stock platforms.
Support layout exploration and visual elements for brand and marketing work.
Keep the idea, context and brand in focus. The tool helps create options; the creative decisions remain mine.
The brand should still feel like itself.
Curiosity matters, but so does consistency. I care about whether an image fits the brand and makes sense for the people seeing it – not simply whether it was made with a new tool.
